parts.partTitle: The extends Keyword & Subclass Memory Layout

beats.headline: Does subclassing create two objects on the heap?
beats.subline: The JVM memory layout for extended classes is simpler and tighter than you think.
beats.narration: When ElectricCar extends Vehicle, does the JVM allocate two separate heap objects? No. The JVM allocates one single unified memory block containing every field from Object, Vehicle, and ElectricCar together.

beats.title: Inheritance vs. Composition

top.label: Is-A (Inheritance)
points: Child safely stands in anywhere parent is expected

bottom.label: Has-A (Composition)
points: Reuses code without class hierarchy coupling
Prevents fragile base class maintenance traps

beats.narration: Inheritance requires passing the strict Is-A test. An ElectricCar is a Vehicle, so inheritance fits cleanly. But a Car is not an Engine—it has an Engine, which requires composition instead.

beats.title: Subclassing and Unified Object Memory

steps.explanation: Fields occupy memory inside every child instance, regardless of private modifier.
JVM packs parent state and subclass fields into one contiguous heap block.

beats.narration: Notice how brand and speedKmh are private in Vehicle, yet they still reside inside every ElectricCar allocation. Private is an access restriction enforced by the compiler, not a memory exclusion rule.

beats.title: Single Inheritance & The Diamond Problem
beats.subtitle: Why Java bans extending multiple class implementation bases

nodes.label: Vehicle Base
nodes.detail: Defines shared maxSpeed field and state

nodes.label: Car & Boat
nodes.detail: Both extend Vehicle with custom state rules

nodes.label: AmphibiousVehicle
nodes.detail: Extends Car, Boat? Banned to stop state clashes!

beats.narration: Java enforces single class inheritance to avoid the diamond problem. If two parent classes defined conflicting fields or methods, a subclass inheriting from both would face ambiguous memory layouts and execution paths.

beats.title: Part 1 Locked In
takeaways: Subclasses allocate ONE contiguous object memory block
Private superclass fields still occupy heap space in child instances
Single class inheritance prevents diamond problem memory collisions

beats.headline: Why does your Java subclass fail to compile?
beats.subline: Forget super(...) when parent lacks default constructor and Java halts immediately.
beats.narration: Ever wonder why your subclass constructor fails to compile? If a superclass defines only parameterized constructors, omitting explicit super calls breaks the build instantly because Java cannot find a default no-args constructor.

beats.title: Constructor Chaining & Java 25 JEP 513

steps.explanation: BaseEntity has no default constructor, requiring explicit super(id) call.
Statements allowed before super(...) provided code does not reference this.

beats.narration: BaseEntity lacks a default constructor, so Account must invoke super explicitly. Modern Java 25 JEP 513 now lets you clean arguments before calling super, as long as you do not access this beforehand.

beats.title: Implicit super() Compilation Failure
beats.caption: What happens when default parent constructors do not exist

lines.text: # Compiling Account.java without explicit super call
Account.java:11: error: constructor BaseEntity in class BaseEntity cannot be applied to given types;

beats.narration: If you omit super, javac automatically inserts an implicit no-args super call. When the parent class lacks a default constructor, compilation halts with a clear signature mismatch error.

beats.title: Delegating to Parent Behavior

steps.explanation: Invokes immediate superclass method to extend behavior rather than overwrite it.

beats.narration: Use super dot start to extend parent behavior instead of replacing it completely. Super targets only your immediate parent—Java explicitly forbids multi-level super calls like super dot super dot start.

beats.title: Constructor Rules Mastered
takeaways: Child constructors execute superclass constructors before child state setup
Java 25 JEP 513 allows argument validation before calling super(...)
super.method() targets only immediate parent implementation levels

beats.headline: Why did your HashSet ignore your equals method?
beats.subline: A single parameter mistake converts an intended override into a silent overload bug.
beats.narration: Writing equals with a custom class parameter looks right, but it silently breaks your collections. Java treats it as an overload, completely bypassing runtime dynamic dispatch when added to a HashSet.

beats.title: Static Overloading vs. Dynamic Overriding

top.label: Overloading (Static Binding)
top.code:
public void send(String msg)
public void send(String msg, int priority)
points: Same method name, different parameter lists
Compiler picks exact signature at compile time

bottom.label: Overriding (Dynamic Dispatch)
points: Exact signature match in subclass hierarchy
JVM resolves method by actual heap object type

beats.narration: Overloading selects methods at compile time based on parameter signatures. Overriding redefines an instance method in a subclass, letting the JVM dispatch calls dynamically at runtime based on the actual heap object.

beats.title: The @Override Safety Net & Covariant Returns

steps.explanation: Object.equals expects Object. Parameter Book creates an overload, missing dynamic dispatch!
Java 5+ permits overriding methods to return a specialized child subtype.

beats.narration: Adding at Override turns silent parameter mismatches into instant compile errors. Also notice covariant return types: an overriding method can return a more specific subclass reference than its parent method.

beats.title: Compiler Enforcement on Overriding Rules
beats.caption: Why access narrowing or broader checked exceptions fail compilation

lines.text: # Attempting to narrow public method to protected in child class
EmailService.java:12: error: send() in EmailService cannot override send() in NotificationService
attempting to assign weaker access privileges; was public
Rule: Can widen access privileges, but NEVER narrow visibility or add checked exceptions!

beats.narration: Java forces strict overriding rules to guarantee substitutability. You can widen access from protected to public, but narrowing visibility or adding new checked exceptions fails compilation immediately.

beats.title: Polymorphism Rules Locked In
takeaways: Always annotate overrides with @Override to prevent static overload bugs
Overriding uses runtime dynamic dispatch; overloading resolves statically
Overriding methods can widen visibility and return covariant subtypes

parts.partTitle: The Cosmic Object Class & equals/hashCode Contract

beats.headline: Why do HashMaps drop entries when keys match?
beats.subline: Overriding equals without hashCode breaks hash-based collections instantly.
beats.narration: Why does HashSet return false for a key you just added? If you override equals without overriding hashCode, equal objects hash to different internal buckets, rendering lookups completely broken.

beats.title: Implementing equals & hashCode Correctly

steps.explanation: Validates type and extracts cast variable safely in a single expression.
Guarantees equal objects calculate identical hash codes for bucket indexing.

beats.narration: Write equals using pattern matching instanceof to verify type and extract fields safely in one step. Then pair it with Objects dot hash to guarantee equal objects produce identical hash codes.

beats.title: The Missing hashCode Bug in JShell
beats.caption: Demonstrating failed set lookups when hashCode is not overridden

lines.text: # Object with custom equals BUT default Object.hashCode
Fix: Equal objects MUST generate identical hashCode values for bucket match!

beats.narration: Here is the exact bug in action. Inserting a key into HashSet works, but querying with an identical value object returns false because default Object dot hashCode routes to the wrong bucket.

beats.title: Core Methods of java.lang.Object
beats.subtitle: Understanding the foundational methods inherited by every Java class

nodes.detail: Human-readable logs & JVM runtime class reflection mirror

beats.narration: Every Java class inherits from Object. Override toString for readable logs, override equals and hashCode for value identity, and leave thread monitor primitives like wait and notify untouched.
